what_happened: The job to make Athena ask root-cause requests for missing stage information before a refusal was rejected at the final verdict. The clippy check failed. One of 7 acceptance criteria was unmet: the criterion that cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass. The one blocker finding says the new test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (lines 3829-3833) trips clippy's field_reassign_with_default lint. The failed check (clippy) and the unmet criterion are separate things. The criterion is unmet because the check failed.
cause: Lint cleanliness is checked only after the producer is done, in the final verification. The producer is not required to run clippy over test code (--all-targets) and fix warnings before it finishes. New test code is where this lint shows up most, because tests often build a default value and then set fields on it. This is the same gap as the earlier cargo fmt class, applied to clippy. The two protections are separate, so fixing fmt did not cover clippy.
prevention: Add a code step at the end of the producer stage. It runs cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings on the working copy. If either fails, the output goes back to the producer for a bounded repair round before the job goes to the verifier. This would stop the whole class of mechanical lint and format failures, not only this lint.
proposed_request: Before a job is handed to the verifier, run cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings on the producer's working copy. If either fails, give the producer the exact output and let it repair in one bounded extra round. Acceptance: (1) a test with a producer diff that has a field_reassign_with_default warning shows the producer is sent the clippy output and the repaired result passes; (2) a clean diff goes straight to the verifier with no extra round; (3) if the repair round still fails, the job records the lint output as the reason. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
